name: Eryngium

project_scope.note: Both species have canonical learner cards. E. yuccifolium retains its unresolved target-zone native-range status; canonical admission is not native-range certification.

study_strategy.warning: Both are spiny Apiaceae and can look 'thistle-like.' Leaf architecture is the fastest split.
look_here_first: Start at mature basal leaves; compare leaf divisions, blade width, venation and spiny margins.
Determine annual taproot versus persistent perennial crown from intact specimens, not isolated cut stems.
Compare same-scale flowering heads: elongate head and projecting bract crown versus pale rounded heads.
If distinguishing from thistles, isolate a flower and fruit; inspect five-parted Apiaceae flower and paired mericarps rather than head silhouette.
overlap_cautions: Both species have spiny foliage or bracts; spines alone do not identify species.
Purple pigmentation can be variable; dried heads lose color.
Young E. yuccifolium may not yet have flowering heads; basal leaves are critical.
Thistles (Asteraceae) can mimic a spiny head but contain composite florets and cypselae rather than separate Apiaceae flowers and paired mericarps.

quick_split: E. leavenworthii — annual; upper plant often purple; broad deeply divided spiny leaves; elongated heads with a conspicuous bract crown.
E. yuccifolium — perennial; long linear yucca-like leaves; pale globose heads; no purple bract crown.
comparison_lesson.caveat: E. yuccifolium remains a range HOLD in this project until a third exact target-zone county is locked.

curation_status.genus_visual_upgrade: two canonical species, five comparison characters, four anatomy roles, photo provenance and restrictions recorded; image pixels not independently verified

source_concept_status.note: Bexar and Gillespie locked; third exact target-zone county still needed.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: Both species: whole plant including basal leaves and flowering stems
E. leavenworthii: basal leaf blade and spiny lobes with scale
E. yuccifolium: straplike basal leaf, venation and margin with scale
Both species: flowering head side view showing subtending bracts
Both species: mature fruit/mericarps and bract details with scale
comparison_cautions: Purple pigmentation is variable and not sufficient for species ID.
Young or cut plants may lack reproductive heads; compare mature basal leaves.
E. yuccifolium remains RANGE_UNRESOLVED in project target-zone metrics despite its canonical learner card.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: photograph basal leaves on an attached flowering stem. Deeply palmately divided, spiny leaves on a short-lived annual point toward E. leavenworthii; long, stiff, narrow, parallel-veined basal blades from a perennial crown point toward E. yuccifolium. Next compare mature head shape and the bract crown; purple coloration alone is not diagnostic.
shared_genus_traits: Apiaceae with dense, bracted flower heads rather than the loose compound umbels typical of many carrot-family plants.
Small individual flowers within each head; inspect a single flower and the mature paired mericarps to distinguish an eryngo head from an Asteraceae capitulum.
Leaves and head bracts are often stiff or spiny; basal leaf architecture is a more dependable first split than head color.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Look at the lowest mature leaves, not just the purple flowering tips. One species has divided spiny blades; the other has long narrow blades with lengthwise veins.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: matched whole basal leaves attached to crown, ruler, and vein close-up

shared_structure_examples.plain: Stiff pointed leaflike pieces form a collar or crown beneath and sometimes beyond each packed flower head.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: matched side-view heads and bracts with scale

shared_structure_examples.plain: A head contains many tiny flowers. Isolate one flower to see separate floral parts above the seed-forming ovary.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: dissected single flower with petals, stamens and ovary at macro scale

shared_structure_examples.plain: The dry fruit divides into two one-seeded halves. This is a family clue that helps separate eryngos from thistles.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: mature fruit intact and separated paired mericarps under magnification
